scope: Full four-file skill review covering fixed sequence versus supported overrides, actual framework/SPI requirements, hook/self-use/super contracts, constructor dispatch, failure/cleanup/async completion, shared-state reentry and compatible composition alternatives.

versions.rationale: No supported content defect identified; no edits and no bump.

findingsRetained.finding: Guidance already starts from consumer/framework requirements, preserves a supported inherited API, compares functions/composition and rejects finalization as a mandatory prerequisite.
findingsRetained.evidence: JLS 17 13.4.17 explicitly documents binary failure when finalization conflicts with an existing override.
findingsRetained.consequence: No blanket migration, visibility narrowing or extra approval step warranted.

findingsRetained.finding: Constructor self-dispatch, required super timing and same-thread reentry are explicit. Distinct invocation state and early rejection are conditional on supported nesting.
findingsRetained.evidence: JLS 17 12.5 and 17.1; the retained synthetic Runner demonstrates nested entry despite synchronized.
findingsRetained.consequence: Existing rules directly select different remedies for the paired policies without forcing composition.

findingsRetained.finding: Business success, failure reporting, cleanup and completion are distinct; start-audit, Error, finish-audit-after-effects and disabled suppression are already qualified.
findingsRetained.evidence: Twenty controls passed, including the unchanged composed example and controlled CompletableFuture continuations. JLS 14 and Throwable/CompletionStage 17 support the boundaries.
findingsRetained.consequence: The text does not claim final executes every step, auditing is cleanup, or all failures imply business rollback.

findingsRetained.finding: Remote outcome, logical operation identity, batch payload, per-item keys and provider contract limit retries; inherited tests do not establish purity, transactions or provider behavior.
findingsRetained.evidence: Stripe idempotency documentation supports the supplied provider-specific illustration; actual provider integration was not executed.
findingsRetained.consequence: No generic retry layer or invariant proof is fabricated by the template or test type.

schemaVersion: 1

name: gof-template-method
version: 1.2.4
description: >-
  Template Method in modern Java: fixing an algorithm's skeleton while named steps vary, and the
  inheritance coupling that often makes composition preferable. Covers when final protects the
  sequence, controlled overriding, minimal hook surfaces, the constructor-calls-an-overridable-method trap,
  protected hooks becoming an API you cannot change, when the pattern is genuinely right
  (frameworks that instantiate your subclass, contract test base classes), and how to convert one
  to a class taking its steps as collaborators. Use when an abstract base class with protected
  hooks is proposed, when a base-class change broke subclasses, when a template has grown past a
  handful of hooks, or when subclasses override the template method itself. Does not cover
  choosing a whole algorithm (gof-strategy), creating the product a template needs
